rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says remembrance occurs only through tongue movement, taking “below loud speech” as secret, quiet verbal remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والجمهور على أن الذكر لا يكون في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds no proof for Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s claim; the verse distinguishes inward remembrance from remembrance by the tongue.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة في ذلك لما زعم بل الظاهر المغايرة بين الحالتين وأنهما ذكران نفساني ولساني

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says speaking below a loud voice deepens sincerity and lies closer to the nature of reflection.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال الزمخشري ومتكلما كلاما دون الجهر لأن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view restricts the two times to the periods when Muslims prayed twice daily, before the five prayers were prescribed.
rows.anchor: فقيل: أراد خصوصية الوقتين لأنهم كانوا يصلون في وقتين قبل فرض الخمس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies al-ghudū with the dawn prayer and al-āṣāl with the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الغدو صلاة الصبح والآصال: صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says dawn and evening are singled out because of their special merit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خصهما بالذكر لفضلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The times may instead mean all times, with the two endpoints expressing the day and night.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى جميع الأوقات وعبر بالطرفين المشعرين بالليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take al-ghudū as the plural of ghudwa, making it plural to match a generic noun in the contrast.
rows.anchor: والغدو، قيل: جمع غدوة فعلى هذا تظهر المقابلة لاسم جنس بجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-ghudū is the verbal noun of al-ghadāʾ, it means the times of early day, balancing one aggregate time span against another.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مصدر الغداء فالمراد بأوقات الغدو حتى يقابل زمان مجموع بزمان مجموع

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Mujliz reads wa-l-īṣāl as a verbal noun of āṣala, meaning entry into the late afternoon, parallel to other verbs for entering a time.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز لا حق بن حميد السدوسي البصري والإيصال جعله مصدرا لقولهم آصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition reinforces the command to remember: maintain remembrance and do not lapse into heedlessness even for an instant.
rows.anchor: ولما أمره بالذكر أكد ذلك بالنهي عن أن يكون من الغافلين أي استلزم الذكر ولا تغفل طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet cannot become heedless because of his protection from error, the prohibition is addressed to him with his community intended.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أنه عليه السلام تستحيل عليه الغفلة لعصمته فهو نهي له صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as being with their Lord are the angels.
rows.anchor: إن الذين عند ربك لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه وله يسجدون هم الملائكة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their nearness to God is nearness in rank and standing, not physical location, reflected in their obedience and pursuit of His pleasure.
rows.anchor: ومعنى العندية الزلفى والقرب منه تعالى بالمكانة لا بالمكان وذلك لتوفرهم على طاعته وابتغاء مرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lack of pride displays servitude and produces obedience; pride instead makes one imagine superiority and prevents obedience.
rows.anchor: نفي الاستكبار عن عبادته وذلك هو إظهار العبودية ونفي الاستكبار هو الموجب للطاعات كما أن الاستكبار هو الموجب للعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their glorification means declaring God transcendent and purifying Him of everything unfitting for His sacred essence.
rows.anchor: إثبات التسبيح منهم له تعالى وهو التنزيه والتطهير عن جميع ما لا يليق بذاته المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view takes the fronted object as restriction: the angels prostrate to Him alone.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور يؤذن بالاختصاص أي لا يسجدون إلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān instead says the object is fronted to make the clause an appropriate verse ending matching the surrounding endings.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه إنما قدم المجرور ليقع الفعل فاصلة فأخره لذلك ليناسب ما قبله من رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship follows from freedom from pride and has inward and bodily forms: glorifying God and prostrating, when the servant is closest to Him.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت العبادة ناشئة عن انتفاء الاستكبار وكانت على قسمين عبادة قلبية وعبادة جسمانية ذكرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a hadith that the heavens creak, with no span except that an angel there is standing, bowing, or prostrating.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث «أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse marks a place for prostration during Qurʾān recitation.
rows.anchor: وله يسجدون هو مكان سجدة وقيل: سجود التلاوة أربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One count recognizes four recitation prostrations: alif-lām-mīm tanzīl, ḥā-mīm tanzīl, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سجود التلاوة أربع سجدات ألم تنزيل وحم تنزيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports ten recitation prostrations, omitting the last of al-Ḥajj, Ṣād, and the three in the short sūras.
rows.anchor: وذكر عن ابن عباس أنها عشر أسقط آخر الحج وص وثلاثا في المفصل

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik's reported count is eleven, omitting the last prostration of al-Ḥajj and the three in the short sūras.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مالك إحدى عشرة أسقط آخرة الحج وثلاث المفصل

rows.speaker: ابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb reports fourteen prostrations, omitting the second prostration in al-Ḥajj.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن وهب أربع عشرة أسقط ثانية الحج

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī count fourteen but differ over the locations: Abū Ḥanīfa omits the second of al-Ḥajj and includes Ṣād; al-Shāfiʿī reverses them.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة والشافعي لكن أبو حنيفة أسقط ثانية الحج وأثبت ص وعكس الشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ibn Ḥabīb also report a count of fifteen, ending with the final prostration of al-ʿAlaq.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن وهب أيضا وابن حبيب خمس عشرة آخرها خاتمة العلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars count sixteen prostrations by adding the prostration in al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء ست عشرة وزاد سجدة الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority hold that recitation prostration is not obligatory; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that it is obligatory.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه ليس بواجب وقال أبو حنيفة هو واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its conditions are those of prayer: purity from impurity and ritual defilement, intention, and facing the qibla; a report in al-Bukhārī permits prostration without purity.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن شرطه شرط الصلاة من طهارة خبث وحدث ونية واستقبال

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī relates from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn al-Munkadir from al-Shaʿbī that one may prostrate without ritual purity.
rows.anchor: إلا ما روى البخاري عن ابن عمر وابن المنكدر عن الشعبي أنه يسجد على غير طهارة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq say to say the takbīr and raise the hands for the prostration.
rows.anchor: وذهب الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق إلى أنه يكبر ويرفع اليدين

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik says to say the takbīr when descending; raising the hands is done in prayer, while reports differ about doing so outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك يكبر لها في الخفض، والرفع في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority say to end with salām; a group of early authorities and Isḥāq say there is no salām.
rows.anchor: ويسلم عند الجمهور، وقال جماعة من السلف وإسحاق: لا يسلم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and a group permit recitation prostration at any time because it is a prayer with a specific cause.
rows.anchor: ووقتها سائر الأوقات مطلقا لأنها صلاة بسبب وهو قول الشافعي وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views forbid it after sunrise until the sun is high, after dawn and afternoon prayers, or only after dawn; these three positions occur in Mālik's school.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما لم يسفر ولم تصفر الشمس، وقيل: لا يسجد بعد الصبح ولا بعد العصر

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The well-known Mālikī position is that one does not perform recitation prostration during an obligatory prayer, whether recited silently or aloud.
rows.anchor: ومشهور مذهب مالك أنه لا يسجد في الفريضة سرا كانت أو جهرا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires prostration from a listener who initially intended to listen.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أبي حنيفة أنه واجب على السامع قصد الاستماع أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the disbelievers' punishment, God offers them a way out: if they abandon disbelief and believe, their past sins are forgiven; disbelief is what they must leave.
rows.anchor: تلطف بهم وأنهم إذا انتهوا عن الكفر وآمنوا غفرت لهم ذنوبهم السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-lladhīna is for conveying a message: the Prophet is ordered to tell them the clause's meaning, whether in its wording or another wording.
rows.anchor: واللام في للذين الظاهر أنها للتبليغ وأنه أمر أن يقول لهم هذا المعنى الذي تضمنته ألفاظ الجملة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the lām as causal, “for their sake”; direct address would instead say “if you desist, We forgive you,” as in Ibn Masʿūd's reading.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري اللام لام العلة، فقال: أي قل لأجلهم هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has yaghfir in the active voice, with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يغفر مبنيا للفاعل والضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return” requires coming back to something left; because they never left disbelief, it means returning to what they could leave, namely fighting the Messenger.
rows.anchor: العود يقتضي الرجوع إلى شيء سابق ولا يكون الكفر لأنهم لم ينفصلوا عنه فالمعنى عودهم إلى ما أمكن انفصالهم منه وهو قتال رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they return to apostasy after having entered Islam; Abū Ḥanīfa explained the verse this way.
rows.anchor: وقيل وإن يعودوا إلى الارتداد بعد الإسلام، وبه فسر أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa uses the verse to argue that an apostate who returns to Islam need not make up worship omitted before or during apostasy.
rows.anchor: واحتج بالآية على أن المرتد إذا أسلم فلا يلزمه قضاء العبادات المتروكة في حال الردة وقبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is consensus that conversion by a non-Muslim combatant removes outstanding liabilities; a protected non-Muslim who converts must still repay human claims, but not God's claims.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن الحربي إذا أسلم لم تبق عليه تبعة وأما إذا أسلم الذمي فيلزمه قضاء حقوق الآدميين لا حقوق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The verse's general address to disbelievers includes the zindīq: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī accept his repentance, while Mālik does not.
rows.anchor: والظاهر دخول الزنديق في عموم قوله قل للذين كفروا فتقبل توبته وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة والشافعي وقال مالك لا تقبل

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī says that if monotheism can erase earlier disbelief, it can certainly erase later sin.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي: التوحيد لا يعجز عن هدم ما قبله من كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is not simply “the precedent of the ancients has passed”; that phrase signals an omitted threat that God will punish and destroy them.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط قالوا: فقد مضت سنت الأولين، ولا يصح ذلك على ظاهره

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The precedent may be the destruction of those punished at Badr or of earlier peoples who conspired against their prophets; Badr is the stronger warning because it was recent and witnessed.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل سنت الأولين أن يراد بها سنة الذين حاق بهم مكرهم يوم بدر وسنة الذين تحزبوا على أنبيائهم فدمروا فليتوقعوا مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Isḥāq support the interpretation that the threat recalls Badr and earlier destroyed nations.
rows.anchor: وتخويفهم بقصة بدر أشد إذ هي قريبة معاينة لهم وعليها نص السدي وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the precedent of the ancients” refers to Badr's earlier participants and past nations: the audience saw Badr's story and heard what befell them.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بقوله سنت الأولين من تقدم من أهل بدر والأمم السالفة والمعنى فقد عاينتم قصة بدر وسمعتم ما حل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-iʿtidhār means disavowing a sin or fault.
rows.anchor: الاعتذار التنصل من الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed etymology derives iʿtidhār from erasure: a person making excuses tries to remove the sin, as in the idiom about houses being erased.
rows.anchor: فقيل: أصله المحو، من قولهم: اعتذرت المنازل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains udhun as a person who believes whatever he hears and accepts everyone's word, named for the organ of hearing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الأذن الرجل الذي يصدق كل ما يسمع

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses udhunan for someone who listens to gossip, illustrating the idiom's sense of a hearer.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: قد صرت أذنا للوشاة سميعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet “an ear” was meant as an insult, portraying him as lacking prudence and easily deceived.
rows.anchor: وهذا منهم تنقيص للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، إذ وصفوه بقلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes udhun to mean “possessor of an ear,” with a genitive noun omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ذو أذن، فهو على حذف مضاف قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it to mean that he has keen hearing and may have heard what they said.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أذن حديد السمع، ربما سمع مقالتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats udhun as a faʿl-form from adhina, “to listen,” like other Arabic forms built on that pattern.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أذن وصف بني على فعل من أذن يأذن أذنا إذا استمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be parsed with an omitted subject: “Say: he is an ear of good for you.”
rows.anchor: أذن على إضمار مبتدأ أي: قل هو أذن خير لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction “ear of good” conveys excellence and goodness, like the expression “a man of truth.”
rows.anchor: وهذه الإضافة نظيرها قولهم: رجل صدق، تريد الجودة والصلاح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the Prophet is an ear for good, truth, and what should be heard and accepted, not for anything else.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد هو أذن في الخير والحق وما يجب سماعه وقبوله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim in one transmission read udhun with nunation and khayr in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وزيد بن علي وأبو بكر عن عاصم في رواية قل: أذن بالتنوين خير بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, udhun and khayr can be successive predicates of an omitted subject; the Prophet is good because he accepts excuses and does not retaliate for bad conduct.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا في أذن أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف، وخير خبر ثان لذلك المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses make khayr an adjective of udhun, a comparative meaning “more good,” or the predicate of an indefinite subject, with an omitted description understood.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون خير صفة لأذن أي: أذن ذو خير لكم. أو على أن خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God explains the Prophet's goodness: one who believes in God fears Him and will not wrongfully harm others.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفه تعالى بأنه يؤمن بالله، ومن آمن بالله كان خائفا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He listens to believers, accepts what they say, and regards them as truthful because they are believers.
rows.anchor: ويسلم لهم ما يقولون ويصدقهم لكونهم مؤمنين، فهم صادقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are singled out although the Prophet is mercy to all worlds because faith gives them a benefit through him that others do not receive.
rows.anchor: وخص المؤمنين وإن كان رحمة للعالمين، لأن ما حصل لهم بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three descriptions explain the Prophet's goodness and show why he is an “ear of good.”
rows.anchor: وهذه الأوصاف الثلاثة مبينة جهة الخيرية، ومظهرة كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم أذن خير

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba regards the bāʾ and lām after the two verbs as extra, yielding the sense “believes God and believes the believers.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: هما زائدان، والمعنى: يصدق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāddah derives from iron, specifically the iron of weapons.
rows.anchor: المحادة مأخوذة من الحديد، حديد السلاح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines muḥāddah as opposition.
rows.anchor: والمحادة هنا، قال ابن عباس: المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are fighting, obstinacy, enmity, or going beyond bounds in opposition; Abū Ḥayyān says these meanings are close.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المحاربة. وقيل: المعاندة. وقيل: المعاداة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read fa-an with fatḥ; the fāʾ answers the condition, and the clause is nominative as an initial clause with its predicate omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فأن له بالفتح، والفاء جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an omitted predicate such as “obligatory”; this is challenged because, under the majority rule, أن cannot precede its predicate.
rows.anchor: فأن له نار جهنم واجب، قاله: الأخفش، ورد عليه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ, and Abū Ḥātim allow أن to begin before its predicate, which lets al-Akhfash parse it by his own rule.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الأخفش والفراء وأبو حاتم الابتداء بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes the clause nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: “the obligation is that he has the Fire.”
rows.anchor: أو في موضع رفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: فالواجب

rows.speaker: الجرمي
rows.claim: Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad treat the second أن as emphatic repetition, with the underlying wording “then he has Hellfire.”
rows.anchor: وقال الجرمي والمبرد: أن الثانية مكررة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates fa-an with anna and supplies an omitted conditional answer, “whoever opposes God and His Messenger perishes”; the clause is then accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون فأن له معطوفا على أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's parse: an omitted conditional answer normally follows a past verb or a present verb with lam, unlike this wording, and the sentence is complete without it.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قدره لا يصح، لأنهم نصوا على أنه إذا حذف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh is reported to analyze the second أن as a substitute for أنه; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that substitution requires the first clause to be complete.
rows.anchor: ونقلوا عن سيبويه أن أن بدل من أنه. قال ابن عطية:

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: The excerpt introduces ʿĀṣim's reading of the conditional clause with “if We forgive a group of you,” in the active voice.
rows.anchor: لعاصم قراءة ... لغيرها مخالفة

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other six of the seven readers use an- taʿfu and tuʿadhdhib, both passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: أن تعف تعذب طائفة، مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads both verbs in the active voice, with God as their subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: إن يعف يعذب مبنيا للفاعل فيهما، أي: إن يعف الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reads both verbs with feminine tāʾ and in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد: إن تعف بالتاء مبنيا للمفعول، تعذب مبنيا للمفعول بالتاء أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains the feminine passive as referring to these sins: “if these sins are forgiven.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: على تقدير إن تعف هذه الذنوب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers masculine agreement because the grammatical subject is an adverbial; the feminine instead follows the sense of showing mercy, which he calls unusual.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الوجه التذكير لأن المسند إليه الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here mujrimīn means persisting in hypocrisy without repentance.
rows.anchor: مجرمين: مصرين على النفاق غير تائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some are of others” describes their shared judgment, rank, and hypocrisy, not literal partiality; they follow one religion and are not believers, as 9:56 says.
rows.anchor: بل بعضهم من بعض في الحكم والمنزلة والنفاق، فهم على دين واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing includes disbelief, worship of other than God, and sins; the people addressed lacked power and visible activity because Islam was ascendant.
rows.anchor: ووصفهم بخلاف ما عليه المؤمنون من أنهم يأمرون بالمنكر وهو الكفر وعبادة غير الله والمعاصي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains “withhold their hands” as refusing to spend in God's cause.
rows.anchor: وقبض الأيدي عبارة عن عدم الإنفاق في سبيل الله قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes the phrase as withholding every kind of good.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: عن كل خير

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says they withhold from jihad and carrying arms against the enemies of religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: عن الجهاد وحمل السلاح في قتال أعداء الدين

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān interprets the phrase as refraining from raising hands in supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان: عن الرفع في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as a metaphor for stinginess with expenditure on obligatory and other good causes.
rows.anchor: وقيل ذلك كناية عن الشح في النفقات في المبار والواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Forgetting” here means abandoning.
rows.anchor: والنسيان هنا الترك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they abandoned obedience to God and His Messenger, so God abandoned them from good, while not forgetting them in punishment.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: تركوا طاعة الله وطاعة رسوله فنسيهم، أي: تركهم من الخير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says they neglected God's remembrance, so He left them without mercy and grace; “forgetting” emphatically expresses abandonment.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أغفلوا ذكره فنسيهم تركهم من رحمته وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the fully realized fāsiqūn, whose rebellion has reached its full extent.
rows.anchor: هم الفاسقون أي: هم الكاملون في الفسق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the earlier peoples were stronger and more numerous, yet disobeyed and perished; the present audience is more liable to destruction in its weakness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: كانوا أشد منكم وأعظم فعصوا فهلكوا، فأنتم أحرى بالإهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: They took their worldly allotment early and left the Hereafter behind, while the present audience followed them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: عجلوا حظهم في دنياهم، وتركوا باب الآخرة، فاتبعتموهم أنتم

words: كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُم بِخَلَاقِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit noun for “those before you” instead of using a pronoun signals belittlement here, just as repetition can elsewhere signal honor.
rows.anchor: وأبرزهم بالاسم الظاهر فقال: كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم، ولم يكن التركيب

words: كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُم بِخَلَاقِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same explicit-noun repetition appears in the rebuke about the devil and in “the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.”
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا وكقوله: إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khudtum means entering into frivolity and falsehood, metaphorically from wading into water; it is used for falsehood because truth proceeds in ordered fashion.
rows.anchor: وخضتم: أي دخلتم في اللهو والباطل، وهو مستعار من الخوض في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a warning that a person who meddles in God's property will face the Fire on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ومنه: رب متخوض في مال الله له النار يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the phrase as “like the wading they did.”
rows.anchor: كالذي خاضوا: أي كالخوض الذي خاضوا قاله الفراء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis means “like the wading of those who waded.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: كالخوض الذين خاضوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation supposes a dropped nūn, giving “like those who waded,” with the sense “like their wading.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: النون محذوفة أي: كالذين خاضوا، أي كخوض الذين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-ladhī with what follows can be construed as a verbal noun, meaning “like their wading.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذي مع ما بعدها يسبك منهما مصدر أي: كخوضهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent of “those” is the earlier peoples described as strong and wealthy, with the present audience's deeds likewise ruined.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أولئك إشارة إلى الذين وصفهم بالشدة وكثرة الأموال والأولاد، والمعنى: وأنتم كذلك يحبط أعمالكم.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows “those” to refer instead to the contemporary hypocrites, with the address shifting; the next verse strengthens that reading.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يريد بأولئك المنافقين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: In this world they suffer hardship and their works are spoiled; in the Hereafter they face Fire without benefit or reward.
rows.anchor: وقوله: في الدنيا ما يصيبهم في الدنيا من التعب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī contrasts the ruined deeds with the statement about Abraham: God gave him his reward in this world and made him righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة، نقيض قوله تعالى: وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says God does not place punishment on the undeserving; the peoples wronged themselves through disobedience and denial until they merited punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي: فما كان الله ليضع عقوبته في غير مستحقها، إذ الظلم وضع الشيء

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī distinguishes divine destruction as what is denied by “wronging them,” and their disbelief and denial as how they wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: ليظلمهم بإهلاكهم، يظلمون بالكفر والتكذيب.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that God's wisdom rules out injustice and punishment without a crime; Abū Ḥayyān identifies this as a Muʿtazilite approach.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فما صح منه أن يظلمهم وهو حكيم لا يجوز عليه القبيح،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān supplies an ellipsis between the messengers' clear signs and the statement that God did not wrong them: they denied the signs, so God destroyed them.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن بين قوله بالبينات. وقوله: فما كان كلاما محذوفا تقديره- والله أعلم- فكذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing the hypocrites' evil qualities, the passage turns to believing men and women and contrasts “some of others” with “some are guardians of others.”
rows.anchor: لما ذكر المنافقين والمنافقات وما هم عليه من الأوصاف القبيحة والأعمال الفاسدة، ذكر المؤمنين والمؤمنات

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the hypocrites have no guardianship or intercession among themselves and do not pray for one another; this verse means guardianship for God's sake.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: إذ لا ولاية بين المنافقين ولا شفاعة لهم، ولا يدعو بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says followers' hypocrisy stems from imitation, nature, and habit, while believers' shared outlook comes from reasoning, divine aid, and guidance; walāya opposes enmity.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: بعضهم من بعض يدل على أن نفاق الأتباع وكفرهم حصل بسبب التقليد لأولئك الأكابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed acts explain guardianship and distinguish believers from hypocrites: believers enjoin right, forbid wrong, pray, give alms, fight, and obey God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: ولما وصف المؤمنين بكون بعضهم أولياء بعض ذكر بعده ما يجري كالتفسير والشرح له، وهي الخمسة

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says Quranic commands to right mean calling from polytheism to Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: كل ما ذكره الله في القرآن من الأمر بالمعروف فهو دعاء من الشرك إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says prohibitions of wrong mean forbidding worship of idols and devils.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر من النهي عن المنكر فهو النهي عن عبادة الأصنام والشياطين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies establishing prayer here with the five prescribed prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ويقيمون الصلاة هي الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ relates from the Prophet that ʿAdn is God's abode, unseen by any eye or heart, inhabited only by prophets, the truthful, and martyrs; God says, “Blessed is whoever enters you.”
rows.anchor: وروى أبو الدرداء عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عدن دار الله التي لم ترها عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report from the Prophet is sound, it must be accepted.
rows.anchor: وإن صح هذا عن الرسول وجب المصير إليه.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Moqātil says ʿAdn is the highest level of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هي أعلى درجة في الجنة.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr describes it as a palace with towers and meadows, five thousand gates, and a beautiful woman at each gate, entered only by a prophet, truthful person, or martyr.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو: قصر حوله البروج والمروج، له خمسة آلاف باب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account describes ʿAdn as a garden with a river and gardens on both banks.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قصته الجنة فيها نهر على حافتيه بساتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account identifies it with al-Tasnīm: palaces of pearl, ruby, and gold, reserved for prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous, whose fragrance reaches five hundred years away.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التسنيم، وفيه قصور الدر والياقوت والذهب، والأرائك عليها الخيرات الحسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the many reports about ʿAdn vary and conflict; accounts restricting it to select groups oppose the verse's promise to believing men and women.
rows.anchor: وهذه أقوال عن السلف كثيرة الاختلاف والاضطراب، وبعضها يدل على التخصيص

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ʿAdn as a proper name, citing “gardens of ʿAdn which the Merciful promised His servants.”
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وعدن علم لقوله تعالى: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the definite relative adjective “which” shows that the noun ʿAdn is definite.
rows.anchor: وإنما استدل بالآية على أن عدنا علم، لأن المضاف إليها وصف بالتي وهي معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that inference is not necessary: the relative clause may predicate an omitted subject, be an accusative specification or praise, or be an apposition to “gardens.”
rows.anchor: ولا يتعين ذلك، إذ يجوز أن تكون التي خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أو منصوبا بإضمار أعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unlikely that “which” modifies “the Garden,” since the apposition “gardens” intervenes; an adjective normally comes before an apposition.
rows.anchor: ويبعد أن تكون صفة لقوله: الجنة للفصل بالبدل الذي هو جنات، والحكم أنه

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ruḍwān with two ḍammas; the reading is a dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ورضوان: بضمتين. قال صاحب اللوامح: وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruḍwān can begin a clause because “from God” qualifies it; its indefinite form means any share of God's pleasure exceeds all the blessings mentioned.
rows.anchor: وجاز الابتداء به لأنه موصوف بقوله: من الله، وأتى به نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing one's master is pleased matters more than the other delights and makes them enjoyable; knowing of his anger spoils them.
rows.anchor: والعبد إذا علم برضا مولاه عنه كان أكبر في نفسه مما وراءه من النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that after the inhabitants settle in Paradise, God offers them His pleasure, promising never to be displeased with them again.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى يقول لعباده إذا استقروا في الجنة: هل رضيتم؟ فيقولون: وكيف لا نرضى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the pleasure and joy of God's approval in their hearts is sweeter and more pleasing than every delight of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: وصل إلى قلوبهم برضوان الله من اللذة والسرور

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees an allusion to the ranks of those near to God and drinking from al-Tasnīm; everyone in Paradise is content, but ranks differ and God's bounty is vast.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويظهر أن يكون قوله تعالى: ورضوان من الله أكبر، إشارة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God's pleasure is the cause of every success and happiness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: رضاه تعالى هو سبب كل فوز وسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” may refer to everything mentioned before or specifically to God's pleasure; the apparent reading refers to all of it.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بذلك إلى جميع ما سبق، أو إلى الرضوان قولان، والأظهر الأول.
